chain.label: Dense wiring and fuel lines behind left instrument panel; PVC insulation
chain.trigger: the densest concentration of wiring in Cessna 310R airplanes is in this area. In addition, fuel lines to instrument panel gauges are routed through this area

chain.label: Unresolved electrical fault in weather radar system or its wiring
chain.trigger: The events on the day before the accident indicate that an electrical problem existed in the weather radar components or related wiring

caused_by.evidence: The weather radar system, which was significant to this accident, was a postmanufacture equipment modification... performed among densely packed layers of wiring of different ages and materials

chain.label: Weather radar failed with burning electrical smell on previous day's flight; CB pulled
chain.trigger: Radar went blank during cruise flight. Recycled - no response...smell of electrical components burning turned off unit - pulled radar [circuit breaker] - smell went away

caused_by.evidence: Pulling the circuit breaker for the weather radar stopped a symptom (the burning smell) of the problem by removing electrical power from the circuit; however, it did not correct the underlying problem

chain.label: No formal NASCAR system or SMS to ground an airplane with an open discrepancy; SOPs disregarded
chain.trigger: there was no formal method for determining and ensuring that an airplane was safe for flight; thus management, maintenance, and flight operations personnel allowed the operation of an airplane with a known and unaddressed discrepancy

chain.label: Airplane released for flight with known discrepancy; no troubleshooting, placard, or collared breaker
chain.trigger: no one examined the airplane to investigate the discrepancy... no company personnel 1) removed the airplane from service; 2) reset the circuit breaker; 3) placed a placard in the cockpit regarding the discrepancy; or 4) deactivated the weather radar system, collaring the associated circuit breaker

caused_by.evidence: the DOM, chief pilot, and aviation director did discuss the weather radar discrepancy writeup, none of these individuals took any actions to ensure that the discrepancy was addressed before agreeing that the airplane could be flown
NASCAR's corporate aviation division's SOPs did not define a procedure for preventing the flight of an airplane with an unaddressed maintenance discrepancy

chain.label: Pilots accepted and flew the airplane with the known unresolved discrepancy
chain.trigger: the pilots accepted the airplane as made available by NASCAR management and maintenance personnel, despite the fact that no diagnostic, corrective, or interim maintenance action had been taken to address the discrepancy

caused_by.evidence: the accident pilots' decision to operate the airplane with that known discrepancy, a discrepancy that likely resulted in an in-flight fire

chain.label: A pilot reset the weather radar circuit breaker without knowing what caused the fault
chain.trigger: it is likely that one of the pilots, consistent with routine and/or the 'Before Starting Engines' checklist for the accident airplane, reset the weather radar circuit breaker, which restored electrical power to the weather radar system's wiring

caused_by.evidence: General aviation pilots often reset circuit breakers during preflight preparations unless the circuit breakers are placarded or collared to show that the associated system is to remain unpowered

The most likely reason for the rapid onset of the problem is that one of the pilots reset the radar circuit breaker, thus reinitiating the development of the problem encountered on the previous flight

chain.label: In-flight fire and smoke forward of the left instrument panel
chain.trigger: smoke in the cockpit we need...to land at Sanford

caused_by.evidence: restored electrical power to the weather radar system's wiring and resulted in the in-flight fire
The flammable fluid lines located near that system's wiring may have provided additional fuel for the fire

chain.label: High-speed emergency descent to low altitude over a residential area
chain.trigger: the airplane was about 3 miles northwest of SFB and descending through about 1,200 feet above ground level

caused_by.evidence: the ATP contacted air traffic control to declare an emergency... The air traffic controller cleared the flight to proceed directly to SFB and descend to 2,000 feet

chain.label: Sudden rapid right turn away from SFB at high speed; cause undetermined
chain.trigger: Just before impact, the airplane entered a 'steep bank' and made a sharp turn to the west

caused_by.evidence: An in-flight fire, especially one located in front of the pilots and directly over their legs, would be very distracting... it is possible that the pilots were distracted by or coping with the in-flight fire
it was not possible to definitively determine the events that led to the accident airplane's maneuvers away from SFB

chain.label: Struck trees, then two homes in a residential area; postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The airplane first struck a north-south line of trees in a right-wing-low attitude at a height of about 65 feet agl... A postcrash fire ensued, destroying the airplane and the second- and third-impacted homes

caused_by.evidence: the airplane subsequently crashed in a residential area about 0.7 nautical miles west of the last primary radar return

chain.label: Both pilots and three people on the ground killed; four seriously injured
chain.trigger: The two pilots on board the airplane... and three people on the ground were killed. Four people on the ground received serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: The autopsy reports indicated that both pilots died as a result of 'multiple blunt force trauma.'
